children: Consumer discretionary companies delivered stronger results against EPS expectations than revenue estimates this week.
Six of nine beat on earnings, but only four topped revenue forecasts. Year-over-year revenue increased at five companies, compared with four that grew EPS.
Here’s a look at how the companies performed:
General Motors
: adj. EPS of $3.70 beats by $0.07; Revenue of $50.02B (+2.9% Y/Y) beats by $1.26B
Genuine Parts Company
: adj. EPS of $2.07 beats by $0.03; Revenue of $6.52B (+4.2% Y/Y) beats by $30M
Hasbro
: adj. EPS of $2.90 beats by $1.05; Revenue of $1.60B beats by $120M.
Tesla
: adj. EPS of $0.48 beats by $0.03; Revenue of $28.05B (-0.1% Y/Y) misses by $200M.
Las Vegas Sands
: adj. EPS of $0.54 misses by $0.14; Revenue of $3.22B (-3.3% Y/Y) misses by $110M.
Tractor Supply Company
: adj. EPS of $0.43 beats by $0.02; Revenue of $3.91B (+5.1% Y/Y) beats by $90M.
PulteGroup
: EPS of $2.53 misses by $0.09; Revenue of $3.98B (-9.5% Y/Y) misses by $170M.
Deckers Outdoor
: EPS of $2.31 beats by $0.52; Revenue of $1.48B (+3.5% Y/Y) misses by $30M.
NVR
: EPS of $89.45 misses by $11.88.; Revenue of $2.35B (-8.0% Y/Y) misses by $100M.
Next week, Amazon
is expected to report EPS of $1.96 on revenue of $202.20B. Ford
is forecast to earn $0.40 per share on revenue of $45.81B, while Starbucks
is expected to post EPS of $0.71 on revenue of $9.24B. Chipotle Mexican Grill
is projected to report EPS of $0.29 on revenue of $3.29B.

title: Consumer Discretionary Earnings: EPS beats outpace revenue
